findings.body: New evidence beyond the prior failure-path review: a batch containing a normal message followed by a session command is consumed under one turn consumer. If processing the earlier message sends partial output and then fails, `handleSessionCommand` deliberately leaves the command pending (`apps/core/src/session/session-commands.ts:366-370`) and returns `success: true`. This branch treats that result as fully handled and releases no item, so the command can never reach the next turn. Release the command's admission item in that path and test the mixed batch.
findings.title: Not done: No message is lost or given twice

findings.body: New evidence beyond the provider-timestamp ordering ruling: a normal message can be received before a slash command whose provider timestamp is older by a second. The take loop consumes both in receive order, but this sort moves the command first. `handleSessionCommand` then handles an immediate command such as `/commands` without processing the normal message (`apps/core/src/session/session-commands.ts:297-300`); both items remain consumed. Preserve admission receive order for the batch.
findings.title: Not done: No message is lost or given twice

findings.body: Ordinary turns now supply `admissionAppId`, but the pre-command and compaction runs built by `createSessionCommandAgentRunners` omit it (`apps/core/src/runtime/group-session-command-runner.ts:38-55`). For a non-default app using a normal channel JID, this fallback selects `default`, so those runs resolve provider configuration and agent session context in the wrong app.
findings.title: Pass the admission app ID to session-command agent runs

findings.body: This hook returns success immediately after writing a continuation file. The file writer only places JSON on disk (`apps/core/src/runtime/continuation-input.ts:65-83`); it does not establish that the model read it. A runner that finishes between the write and its next read can leave an applied command whose item remains consumed, because normal finalization releases only pending continuations (`apps/core/src/runtime/live-turn-authority.ts:523-541`). The story assigns runner delivery IDs and release of unconfirmed commands to T4, so this remains a T4 dependency.
findings.title: Later: T4 must confirm runner delivery before retaining follow-up input
